lead: "This 11-day itinerary combines Cusco and Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca and the Amazon rainforest near Iquitos. It begins with historic cities and highland scenery, followed by 3 days of boat travel and accommodation at a lodge on the Amazon."
---

## One itinerary: ancient Peru, a high-altitude lake and the Amazon

The “Enchanting Peru + Iquitos” tour lasts **11 days** and combines 3 experiences: Inca heritage sites, highland landscapes around Lake Titicaca and tropical rainforest beside the Amazon River. It begins in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), continues to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), reaches [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and ends after an Amazonian stage via [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/).

The combination suits travelers eager to explore several very different parts of Peru in one trip, who are comfortable with hotel changes, domestic flights and boat transfers. It is a more active itinerary than staying in one national park or visiting Machu Picchu alone.

Included are flights Lima–Cusco, Juliaca–Lima and Lima–Iquitos–Lima, transfers, specified excursions with a Russian-speaking guide and round-trip Expedition-class train tickets to Aguas Calientes.

## The Andes and Titicaca before the jungle

A sightseeing tour of [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is followed by a trip to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Train arrival and the entry time for your selected route through the archaeological site should be coordinated in advance.

On day 4, you may remain in Cusco or take an additional excursion into the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). It is **a separately paid option**, not a compulsory tour component. Review the daily program carefully: a geographical name on the itinerary does not necessarily indicate an included activity.

Travel continues by bus from Cusco to Puno. On [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the itinerary visits the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and [Taquile Island](/peru/place/taquile-island/). Prepare for the altitude and chilly morning hours, particularly after a long transfer.

## The Amazonian days near Iquitos

After returning to Lima, travelers fly to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/). From the city, they continue to the port and take a speedboat to Heliconia Amazon River Lodge near Yanamono. The lodge offers jungle walks; subsequent activities include birdwatching, fishing on the Amazon, searching for pink river dolphins and learning about giant water lilies.

Full board is listed for the Amazonian stage. Wildlife sightings nonetheless depend on natural conditions. Birds, dolphins and other inhabitants of the river move freely in their habitat, so no particular encounter can be guaranteed.

Boat journeys, humid conditions and tropical vegetation call for different equipment from the highlands. Quick-drying clothes, rain protection, shoes suitable for wet trails and waterproof protection for belongings are useful. Choose your travel period with the rainy season and changing river levels in mind, as these influence river excursions.

## What to check before departure

The main organizational challenge is coordinating connections between Lima, Cusco, Juliaca and Iquitos. Domestic air tickets are included, but the exact flights and baggage allowances must be checked against the confirmed program.

Another consideration is changing climates: cool Andean evenings, sunny high-altitude days and the humid Amazon require different clothes in one suitcase. Take it easy after flying into Cusco; on arrival in the jungle, account for lodge arrangements and the length of the river transfer.

If you are primarily interested in wildlife and tropical ecosystems, also explore our [wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/). If ancient Inca cities are your priority, see our [cultural journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) and compare the time devoted to archaeology.

## Frequently asked questions about “Peru + Iquitos”

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes. Visiting [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is part of the main program. The train to Aguas Calientes is listed among the inclusions.

### Is the Sacred Valley included in the price?

No. Day 4 offers a choice between free time in Cusco and a separately paid optional excursion to the Sacred Valley.

### How much time is spent in the Amazon?

Arrival in Iquitos and transfer to the lodge take place on day 7. Day 8 features river and forest activities; on day 9, after the lodge program, the itinerary returns to Lima.

### Can you see pink river dolphins?

Searching for them is mentioned in the Amazonian day, but encounters with wildlife depend on the weather, water levels and animal behavior.

## A 6-day Peru tour: your first introduction to the country

**The Lima–Cusco–Machu Picchu–Sacred Valley itinerary suits travelers seeking the main Inca monuments without spending several weeks away.** Over 6 days, it combines the Pacific-coast capital, a high-altitude city and a trip to the celebrated citadel. Unlike trekking expeditions, it includes transfers, train travel and standard sightseeing excursions.

Its defining feature is a compact schedule: one journey includes a city day in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), a flight to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), a dedicated day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and an excursion to the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). Six days are not enough for an unhurried exploration of Peru, but they make sense for a first visit focused on history.

## How the sightseeing days are arranged

| Day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Lima, museum and historic center |
| 3 | Cusco and Inca monuments |
| 4 | Machu Picchu by train |
| 5 | Sacred Valley |
| 6 | Transfer to the airport |

The first day allows time for an airport welcome, hotel check-in and rest. Sightseeing in Lima covers oceanfront Miraflores, the historic center and the Larco Museum. In one city, you can encounter traces of pre-Columbian cultures and the Spanish colonial period.

In Cusco and its surroundings, the focus shifts to Inca architecture: major stone structures, sacred places and city monuments. A separate day is devoted to the Sacred Valley, with stops at [Urubamba](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/). This shows how farming, settlements, roads and religious centers were connected within the Inca Empire.

## Train to Machu Picchu: what is included?

On day 4, travelers take an **Expedition-class** tourist train to [Aguas Calientes](/peru/place/aguas-calientes/), then continue to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The price includes round-trip rail tickets for Cusco–Aguas Calientes–Cusco, along with entrance tickets to sightseeing sites.

Agree separately on **the precise date, entry time and circuit available within the citadel**. Peru's Ministry of Culture issues tickets for particular routes and timeslots; one ticket does not allow unrestricted access to all open and closed sections. When booking, decide whether special panoramic areas are important or the usual guided circuit is sufficient.

In this program, the train is primarily transport to the citadel and back to Cusco. Travelers who value fine dining aboard the train and restaurant-car service may prefer Ada Tours' other [6-day Hiram Bingham itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/). The destination is the same, but the rail experience differs.

## Cusco's altitude and the pace of the first mountain days

Cusco is more than 3,300 m above sea level. Arriving from coastal Lima brings noticeably different conditions, potentially including fatigue and altitude-adjustment symptoms. This tour schedules archaeological sites near the city for the afternoon of arrival, so assess your altitude tolerance and discuss the pace before departure.

Sensible preparation includes resting after the flight, drinking enough water and avoiding strenuous activity during the first hours. Existing medical conditions or acclimatization difficulties call for individual advice from a doctor. Machu Picchu lies lower than Cusco, but its steps and terraces still require comfortable shoes and some stamina.

## Who is this short itinerary for?

The tour particularly suits archaeology and culture enthusiasts who want to visit Peru's major historical monuments in one program. The tightest stage is flying to Cusco and then sightseeing. For more rest, a leisurely exploration of the valleys or wildlife watching, consider [longer Peru tours](/peru/tour/).

Consider more than the weather when selecting dates. Holidays, busy trains and limits on Machu Picchu admissions can affect convenient timeslots. For a fixed schedule, confirmed rail arrangements and access to the citadel matter more than broad promises about the “right season.”

## Inclusions and expenses: what to check before booking

The tour includes transfers and excursions, a Russian-speaking guide, an Expedition-class train ticket and admission tickets to excursion sites. Meals are included to the extent specified in the program. Airport fees, optional excursions, possible excess baggage charges, alcoholic beverages and soft drinks are listed separately.

Given the 6-day duration, check the arrival time of your international flight, domestic connections and the exact sequence of the train excursion. Even when the places visited are identical, these factors can substantially change the amount of free time available.

## Frequently asked questions about the Lima–Cusco–Machu Picchu tour

### Must you buy your own train ticket to Machu Picchu?

No. The published program includes an Expedition-class round-trip ticket. The departure date and citadel admission are coordinated when booking.

### Can you see Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley in 6 days?

Yes. They are 2 separate sightseeing stages: the Machu Picchu train excursion is on day 4, and the Sacred Valley with several monuments occupies day 5.

### Is there time to acclimatize?

There is a little time after arriving, but sightseeing is already scheduled for the afternoon of the first day in Cusco. Travelers sensitive to altitude should discuss the itinerary's pace in advance.

### What language is used for guiding?

The included services specify excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. This differs from tours where group excursions are conducted in English or Spanish.

lead: >-
  This 14-day route links Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Titicaca and Arequipa with archaeological sites in northern Peru. Its chief distinguishing feature is the northern extension: Trujillo, Chan Chan, Chiclayo and the legacy of the Lord of Sipán. Discover who this itinerary is for, how flights are arranged and which visits are optional.
---

## Why this 14-day Peru tour goes beyond the usual Inca route

The first stage connects [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). It introduces Inca history, colonial cities and the highland nature of the Andes.

**This program stands apart through its northern archaeological extension.** After returning to Lima, the itinerary continues to [Trujillo](/peru/place/trujillo/) and [Chiclayo](/peru/place/chiclayo/). These areas contain monuments of cultures that existed before the Spanish arrived and differed from Inca civilization. This route suits travelers curious about several historical periods and museums rather than only the famous Machu Picchu citadel.

If northern Peru is not essential, Ada Tours offers a [12-day alternative covering Cusco, Titicaca, Colca and Arequipa](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/). The distinction lies in specific places and transfers, not an abstract notion of one journey being more “complete.”

## Northern coast: Chan Chan and the Lord of Sipán

[Chan Chan](/peru/place/chan-chan/) was the capital of the Chimú kingdom. UNESCO describes it as the largest pre-Columbian city made of earth-based building materials in the Americas. Its mudbrick walls, extensive complexes and geometric layout contrast with Inca stone architecture, an especially rewarding comparison for history enthusiasts.

Near Trujillo, the program includes the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, associated with the earlier Moche culture, and the Huanchaco coast. The following day around [Chiclayo](/peru/place/chiclayo/), visitors explore museum collections dedicated to the Lord of Sipán and the [Huaca Rajada](/peru/place/huaca-rajada/) archaeological site. Excavations and museum discoveries illustrate local concepts of power, burial traditions and artistic craftsmanship.

These are packed sightseeing days. The northern itinerary involves an evening bus transfer after the Trujillo sites and a flight back to Lima after the Chiclayo visits. Choose these days for their historical content, not as a chance to spend 2 extra relaxed days at the seaside.

## Flights and the longest transfers

Included domestic flights are **Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, Lima–Trujillo and Chiclayo–Lima**. Travel between Trujillo and Chiclayo is by bus. The northern extension adds real transport segments and a change of overnight accommodation.

The Andes also bring a long journey: the bus from Cusco to Puno passes historical sites, a lunch stop and the high-altitude La Raya Pass. The journey takes almost a full day. An optional Titicaca Train journey is offered instead for an additional charge. The substitution concerns only Cusco–Puno; other road transfers remain unchanged.

The journey to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) uses the railway, and an **Expedition-class** ticket is listed among the inclusions. Plan your date by coordinating the train, available entry circuit and return to Cusco. The round trip fills much of the day.

## Altitude and wellbeing: what changes after Lima?

From the Pacific coast, the route climbs rapidly to Cusco at approximately 3,350 m, then proceeds to Lake Titicaca at around 3,800 m. Travel to [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) crosses high-altitude areas before descending toward Arequipa.

Even ordinary sightseeing may feel harder at these elevations. During the first days after flying into Cusco, avoid intense activity and monitor your wellbeing. If you have cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, or have previously struggled with altitude, consult a doctor before buying the trip.

The Titicaca stage introduces the floating Uros Islands. In the Colca area, a visit to the Cruz del Condor viewpoint is planned; sightings of condors depend on nature and weather. Rest is particularly valuable after long bus journeys.

## Which visits are optional despite appearing in the description?

A free day in Lima offers a separate excursion to Paracas, the Ballestas Islands and a flight over the Nazca Lines. **Nazca is not a compulsory destination in the main 14-day itinerary.** Consider whether the outing fits your available day, flight-weather restrictions and desire to rest after the Andes.

Other optional visits include Cusco Cathedral, the Titicaca Train and the Larco Museum on departure day from Lima if schedules allow. Some options specify individual surcharges; mentioning them does not make them included services.

If cultural attractions matter most to you, see our [cultural and historical Peru tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). Compare the actual itineraries, considering duration, domestic transport and optional activities.

## Who should choose this route?

**A 14-day journey including northern Peru** suits those who want to combine Inca heritage, Chimú culture and the archaeological discoveries of Sipán. Expect early departures, several flights, high-altitude sightseeing and a busy program.

If your main interests are Machu Picchu, the highland lake and Colca scenery, the [12-day option](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) covers these without the northern extension. Compare shorter and longer tours in the [Peru catalog](/peru/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 14-day Peru tour

### How does the northern section differ from Cusco and Machu Picchu?

Around Trujillo and Chiclayo, visitors mainly encounter Chimú and Moche heritage, including Chan Chan and the Sipán sites. Cusco and Machu Picchu focus primarily on the Incas.

### Is the Nazca Lines flight included?

No. Paracas, the Ballestas Islands and the flight over the Nazca Lines are an optional excursion on the free day in Lima.

### Which flights are included?

The listed inclusions specify 4 domestic flights: Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, Lima–Trujillo and Chiclayo–Lima. Exact departure times and international connections depend on your booking.

### Is the program suitable for someone sensitive to altitude?

Discuss it individually with a doctor. The itinerary moves quickly from the coast into the Andes, and the Titicaca area sits at approximately 3,800 m. Ordinary walks and bus tours do not eliminate altitude-sickness risks.

## What you will see in Peru in 12 days

The main itinerary connects [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). Across one journey, travelers experience different historical periods, landscapes and altitudes, from the Pacific coast to Andean towns and rural settlements.

This option is particularly attractive for the **wide-ranging geography of southern Peru**. It suits those interested in Inca monuments, colonial cities, the high-altitude lake and condor watching. Yet 12 calendar days are not 12 full sightseeing days. The itinerary includes domestic flights, the journey from Cusco to Puno, the transfer to Colca and the return to Lima.

Nazca is also mentioned in the tour's title. However, the visit to Paracas and the Ballestas Islands and the flight over the Nazca Lines are **optional activities on a free day**, not part of the compulsory itinerary. If Nazca is the main reason for choosing the tour, clarify this option beforehand.

## Where does traveling take the most time?

The group flies from Lima to Cusco, then visits Machu Picchu by train, returning the same day, and has a separate day in the Sacred Valley. An **Expedition-class** train ticket is listed among the included services.

Between Cusco and Puno, the itinerary schedules a bus journey lasting roughly 10 hours. Stops include Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, a stop near Sicuani, La Raya Pass and Pucará. It is a fascinating route through history and mountain scenery but occupies nearly the whole day and requires many hours in transit.

The **Titicaca Train** may be selected as an optional alternative to the bus. This changes arrangements for that one section. Operating days and a surcharge are listed for the option, but actual availability must be checked for your travel date.

The next overland stage runs from [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to [Colca](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), followed by an overnight stay near Chivay and onward travel to Arequipa. Consider your tolerance for long road journeys before booking. The main domestic flights Lima–Cusco and Arequipa–Lima are included.

## Altitude in Cusco and at Titicaca: what to consider

Elevation is one of this trip's defining features. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) lies around 3,350 m above sea level, and Lake Titicaca about 3,800 m. Flying from Lima rapidly transports travelers into conditions of reduced atmospheric pressure.

Headaches, fatigue and other symptoms may occur at these altitudes even in people without mountaineering experience. During the first days in the mountains, conserve energy, reduce exertion and pay attention to how you feel. Those with chronic medical conditions or a history of altitude sickness should consult a doctor before traveling.

Altitude matters beyond walking. Early departures and long transfers are planned between Cusco, Puno and Colca. A measured pace and sufficient sleep may do more for comfort than adding another optional excursion.

## Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley: two sides of Inca heritage

Visiting [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) focuses on the renowned high-altitude archaeological complex. The program includes a transfer to the railway station, train travel, a guided visit and return to Cusco. The precise entrance circuit and timeslot should be confirmed separately because they determine site access and the day's timing.

The [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) provides a broader introduction to Inca heritage. Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero and the agricultural terraces at Moray are mentioned. Visitors see settlement layouts, crafts and agricultural history rather than a single extraordinary monument.

Both days are busy. Travelers wishing to explore archaeological sites in detail should consider whether enough time is available and discuss individual program adjustments if needed. Similar options appear among our [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

## Titicaca and Colca: nature and wildlife observation

At [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the program visits the floating Uros Islands and introduces the residents' traditions. Both the lakeside landscape and human history matter: how reed islands and boats are built, and how crafts are practiced.

Around [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), the route includes highland lakes, viewpoints and Cruz del Condor. Flamingos may be seen near Lagunillas, while condors can be observed over Colca. Wild birds do not follow a tourist schedule, and sightings depend on the weather and animal behavior.

When comparing tours, distinguish a scheduled visit to a site from a guaranteed wildlife sighting. A stop at the viewpoint is confirmed in the itinerary, but no particular number of birds at a specific time can be promised.

## Optional visits and free time in Lima

After returning from Arequipa, the itinerary offers some free time in Lima. It may be used for rest or an optional trip to Paracas, the Ballestas Islands and the Nazca Lines. Such a journey takes up much of the day and requires separate arrangements for the flight.

The Larco Museum is also mentioned as a possible visit on departure day if flight times allow. The museum visit is paid separately. Before an international flight, allow enough time for the road journey, baggage and airport formalities.

The included-services list mentions the Feast of the Virgin of Candelaria, but the tour listing provides neither departure dates nor an exact festival day. If attending the event is your objective, **first confirm the dates and participation plan**. Do not assume the festival is included on every departure.

## How it differs from the 14-day itinerary

The [14-day tour with Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/) shares much of the Andean portion but extends into northern Peru. It includes Chan Chan, Sipán monuments and additional domestic flights, appealing to travelers interested in pre-Inca cultures of the northern coast.

The **12-day itinerary** focuses on Lima, Cusco, Titicaca, Colca and Arequipa without the northern extension. Road travel remains substantial. Compare alternatives in the [Peru tour catalog](/peru/tour/), checking actual sightseeing days and included transport.

## Frequently asked questions about the 12-day Peru journey

### Is the flight over the Nazca Lines included in the main price?

No. Paracas, the Ballestas Islands and the Nazca Lines flight are optional activities for the free day in Lima.

### Can you take a train from Cusco to Puno?

Yes. The description offers the Titicaca Train as an optional alternative for a surcharge. Check whether it runs on your travel date.

### Is difficult trekking compulsory?

No multi-day trek is part of the main program. However, archaeological-site walks, long transfers and high-altitude overnight stays require attention to wellbeing.

### Does this tour visit Chan Chan and Chiclayo?

No. Those northern sites are included in the [14-day version with Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/).

## Excursions to Urubamba and the Sacred Valley from Cusco

[Urubamba](/peru/place/urubamba/) is in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), surrounded by agricultural fields, mountains and settlements. It is one stop in discovering the valley, where ancient history coexists with everyday life.

In the Ada Tours catalog, Urubamba features in the [“Sacred Valley of the Incas” excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/). Departure is from Cusco, and Urubamba forms part of a wider itinerary rather than being the only destination. Check the number of stops and decide which interest you most.

## What the Sacred Valley tour includes

The itinerary visits Urubamba, Pisac, [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), Moray and Awanacancha. These places highlight different aspects of the valley: archaeology, agricultural terraces, traditional settlements and modern rural life.

In Urubamba, visitors see a thriving town and the fields around it. Pisac is known for archaeology and local handicrafts. Ancient terraces and the historic street plan are highlights of [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/). [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) blends Inca and colonial architecture. Moray is distinguished by its circular agricultural terraces.

At Awanacancha, visitors encounter llamas, alpacas and vicuñas and learn about local wool-working traditions. The program includes lunch at Tunupa restaurant. The exact order of visits and paid-for services should be checked in the specific offer.

| Stop | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Urubamba | Town and valley agriculture |
| Pisac | Archaeology and crafts |
| Ollantaytambo | Stone terraces |
| Chinchero | Inca and colonial history |
| Moray | Circular terraces |
| Awanacancha | Llamas and alpacas |

All these places are on the [Sacred Valley excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/), but the trip does not allocate equal time to each and cannot guarantee arbitrary changes.

## A sightseeing day trip or an overnight stop?

A one-day overview is convenient for a first visit when you want to see several places along the valley. Its main advantage is variety, while time at each stop is limited by the total duration.

If Urubamba itself, walks around the town and leisurely exploration of rural life interest you, consider staying in the valley for a few nights. But **an overnight stay is not included in this standalone excursion**. Such a program must be arranged as part of a separate [Peru tour](/peru/tour/).

For deeper insight into Inca architecture, also set aside extra time for [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) and [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/). A short stop on a general tour and an independent walk serve different purposes.

## Logistics from Cusco: altitude and transfers

The excursion departs from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Travel follows mountain roads; actual times depend on the selected stops, weather and road conditions. On a packed itinerary, determine in advance where longer walks are planned and where the stops are brief.

Many Sacred Valley settlements lie lower than Cusco. This can inform planning of the first days in the Andes, but the elevation difference does not replace acclimatization. Adjust the pace to your wellbeing, age and trip duration.

Bring comfortable footwear, water, sun protection and clothing for weather changes. Wet-season trails and mountain roads call for additional caution. Check archaeological-site opening hours and visiting rules for the precise dates.

## Services and prices

The [“Sacred Valley of the Incas” excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) is listed with a starting price in US dollars, but the amount does not automatically apply to every possible arrangement. This excursion can be added to a journey. Confirm transport, guiding language, admission tickets, meals, meeting point and group terms in the final agreed offer.

If you plan to continue to Machu Picchu or spend several days in the Sacred Valley, coordinate the visit sequence with the rest of your trip to avoid repeating scheduled stops.

Compare other possibilities in our [Peru excursion catalog](/peru/excursion/) and [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Urubamba excursions

### Is there an excursion to Urubamba from Cusco?

Yes. The [Sacred Valley of the Incas excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) begins in Cusco and includes Urubamba among its stops.

### Can you see Ollantaytambo and Chinchero in the same trip?

Yes. Both sites are included in the [Sacred Valley route](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/). Stop durations are confirmed separately.

### Is a hotel in Urubamba included?

The standalone excursion is not described as an overnight journey. If you want to stay here, arrange accommodation within a separate tour.

### Which is better for a first visit: one day or several?

A one-day overview introduces several key sites. Several days allow fewer stops per day and more time in the settlements you enjoy.

### Can this excursion start in Urubamba itself?
